tīhamata: [Tīha+mata] (ti) CL=7 (A dead body) who is dead before three days.
tīhapaṭiggahita: [Tīha+paṭiggahita] (ti) CL=7 It has been accepted for three days, (Butter, etc.,) are accepted for three days.
tīhappaṭicchanna: [Tīha+paṭicchanna] (ti) CL=7 (A) It should be covered for three days. (B) It is covered or concealed for three days. See - Ekāhappaṭicchanna (pācita, yo, 2. 17). (C) (Āpatatti) that is concealed for three days.
tīhidhammehisutta: [Tīhidhammehi+sutta] (na) CL=7 Tīhidhammehi sutta, A sutta that preaches about: A woman who is jealous in the morning, is envious in the evening, has an attachment at night, and if she has these three kinds of evil dhammas, when she passes away she will reach the Hell.
tīra: [Tīra+a] (na) CL=7 [Dhāna, ṭī. 664. Niti, dhā. 336. Dhātvattha. 164. Tā+ra=raka. Ṇvādi. 145.] (1) A bank (of a river), (A) On this bank. (B) Another bank. (2) It looks like this bank, (A) Tebhūmakavaṭṭa. (B) Six kinds of Ajjhattikāyatana. (C) Sakkāyadiṭṭhi = The doctrine that happens on the obvious five aggregates embodying a being. (D) Ten kinds of Adhamma such as Micchādiṭṭhi. (E) Lokī dhamma. (3) It looks like another bank, (A) Nibbāna. (B) Six kinds of Bāhirāyatana. (C) Upright dhamma. See - Tīragocara. (D) Ten kinds of dhamma such as sammādiṭṭhi. (E) Lokuttarā dhamma. (4) It has an end. See also - Tīrantaruhavātīra. (Ti) (5) (River, etc.,) that has the bank.
tīradassana: [Tīra+dassana] (ti) CL=7 (Buddha) who sees the bank that is Nibbāna which is the end of samsara.
tīradassī: [Tīra+disa+ṇī] (ti) CL=7 (A) (A crow) who sees the bank of (an ocean). (B) One who concentrates and contemplates this bank as suffering cyclic (due to past misdeeds).
tīragocara: [Tīra+gocara] (ti) CL=7 One who wanders on this bank (of upright dhamma), and is wandering on the wholesome dhamma.
tīragāma: [Tīra+gāma] (pu) CL=7 A village on the shore, A waterfront village.
tīramariyādabandha: [Tīramariyādā+bandha] (ti) CL=7 (Water) which is closed and formed by the bank.
tīranta: [Tīra+anta] (pu,na) CL=7 (A) Near a bank, Shoreline, Strand. (A shoreline) that is the end which is a bank.
tīrantaruha: [Tīranta+ruha] (pu) CL=7 A Bankside tree (or) A tree grows on the bank.
tīrapariyāya: [Tīra+pariyāya] (pu) CL=7 The deception of Tīrasaddā, A Saddā which is the same meaning as Tīrasaddā (such as Velā)
tīrappadesa: [Tīra+padesa] (pu) CL=7 (A) Another side bank (that is Nibbāna). (B) The place where is the bank (river, etc.,).
tīrasama: [Tīra+sama] (ti) CL=7 It is the same as the bank.
tīrayanta: [Tīra+ṇaya+anta] (ti) CL=7 One who can be concentrated and contemplated.
tīrayati: [Tīra+ṇaya+ti] (kri) CL=7 (A) It makes a decision. See also - Tīreti (B). (B) It thinks. See - Tīreti (D). (C) It concentrates and contemplates. See also - Tīreti (A).
tīrayitvā: [Tīra+ṇaya+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) Having contemplated and made a decision. (B) Having considered. (C) Having spread. (D) (D) Having criticized and distinguished.
tīraṇa: [Tīra+yu] (na,thī) CL=7 (1) (A) Made a decision. (B) Concentration and contemplation. (2) (A) It is a cause of making a decision. (Wisdom) which is the cause of concentration and contemplation.
tīraṇabāhulla: [Tīraṇa+bāhulla] (na) CL=7 It"s a lot of concentration and contemplation.
tīraṇapariññattha: [Tīraṇapariññā+attha] (ti) CL=7 It has (Ñātapariññā) benefit that is Tīraṇapariññā.
tīraṇapariññā: [Tīraṇa+pariññā] (thī) CL=7 (1) (A) It can be distinguished and known by concentration and contemplation. (B) It knows clearly by making a decision. (2) (A) It is a cause of knowing clearly by concentration and contemplation. (B) (Wisdom) that is a cause of knowing clearly by concentration and contemplation.
tīraṇapariññābyāpāra: [Tīraṇapariññā+byāpāra] (pu) CL=7 It is heavy contemplation and perception of Tīraṇapariññā.
tīraṇapariññādhiṭṭhāna: [Tīraṇapariññā+adhiṭṭhāna] (ti) CL=7 (Pahānapariññā) that has a dependent place which is Tīraṇapariññā.
tīraṇarasa: [Tīraṇa+rasa] (ti) CL=7 (A) It has the matter that has made a decision. (B) (Wisdom) which has the concentrated and contemplated matter.
tīraṇavibhūta: [Tīraṇa+vibhūta] (ti) CL=7 It overcomes the form by concentration and contemplation on the form (that doesn"t attach with Chanda and Rāga).
tīraṇavipassanā: [Tīraṇa+vipassanā] (thī) CL=7 "Vipassanā Wisdom" is special meditation by concentration and contemplation.
tīraṇaṭṭha: [Tīraṇa+attha] (pu) CL=7 (A) It has the meaning of concentration and contemplation. (B) Nature of contemplation.
tīraṭṭha: [Tīra+ṭhā+a] (ti) CL=7 (The base of a bridge, etc.,) that set up and supported the bank.
tīrenta: [Tīra+ṇe+anta] (ti) CL=7 (A) Can be contemplated. (B) Can be considered and judged.
tīresi: [Tīra+ṇe+ī] (kri) CL=7 They have made a decision. See - Tīreti (B).
tīretabba: [Tīra+ṇe+tabba] (ti) CL=7 (A) Should be concentrated and contemplated. (B) It should be made a decision. (C) Should be overcome. See - Atīraṇeyya.
tīreti: [Tīra+ṇe+ti] (kri) CL=7 [Nīti, dhā. 336.] (A) It concentrates and contemplates. (B) It makes a decision. (C) It considers. (D) It thinks.
tīretvā: [Tīra+ṇe+tvā] (kri,vi) CL=7 (A) Having concentrated and contemplated. (B) Having made a decision.
tīreyya: [Tīra+ṇe+eyya] (kri) CL=7 (A) It should be concentrated and contemplated. (B) It should be made a decision. See - Tīreti.
[Tīra+ṇe+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 It should consider. See - Tīreti-(C).
tīreyyaṃ: [Tīra+ṇe+eyyaṃ] (kri) CL=7 It should consider. See - Tīreti-(C).
tīreyyātha: [Tīra+ṇe+eyyātha] (kri) CL=7 They made a decision. See - Tīreti (B).
tīrita: [Tīra+ta] (ti) CL=7 (A) It should be concentrated and contemplated. (B) It makes a decision.
tīritadhamma: [Tīrita+dhamma] (ti) CL=7 (An Arahant) who has the concentrated and contemplated dhamma.
tīya: [Yadicchānāma] (pu) CL=7 One who was named Tīya. See also - Brāhmaṇatissa.
tīyati: [Ti+ya+ti] (kri) CL=7 It cuts off and quiet. See - Yati.
tīṇikkhattuṃ: [Tīṇi+kkhattuṃ] (bya) CL=7 [Vibhatyanta puda- Kkhattuṃ-paccaya]. Three times, Three turns.
tīṇuppalamāliya: [Ti+uplalamālā+iya] (ti) CL=7 (A Thera) was named Tīṇuppalamāliya who offered three lotus flowers, (A) A Thera who offered three lotus flowers to Lord Buddha Vipassī. (B) A Thera who offered three lotus flowers to Lord Buddha Phussa. See original.
tīṇikkhattu: [Tīṇi+kkhattuṃ] (bya) CL=7 [Vibhatyanta puda- Kkhattuṃ-paccaya]. Three times, Three turns.
